newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Dec 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Dec 11.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- VW CHIEF DENTS HOPES FOR PEACE IN GM FEUD

Hopes that had been rising of an amicable settlement to a long-running dispute between Volkswagen and General Motors appear to have been dashed by the refusal of the German auto manufacturer's chairman Ferdinand Piech to apologise over his role in the affair. A number of legal suits between the two parties are pending following claims by GM that a parting executive had taken confidential documents with him to rival Volkswagen. In an interview to be published on Thursday in Stern, Piech stresses that he has nothing to apologise about.
-- NORTHERN ELECTRIC MERGER PLAN

Details have been revealed by Northern Electric, the subject of a hostile takeover bid from CalEnergy of the US, of plans for an increase in dividend payments and a merger of its electricity and gas supply divisions with another electricity company, believed to be London Electricity. The company's 1998 dividend is to rise 17 per cent to 50p per share, with subsequent annual rises of 7 per cent planned. The announcements are reported to have made the outcome of the CalEnergy bid less certain than was previously the case.
-- RJB SHARES SLIDE ON THREAT FROM CHEAP COAL IMPORTS

Shares in RJB Mining, the company that acquired most of former British Coal's pits, have fallen sharply in value after broker BZW noted that it might have to reduce prices in order to fend off competition presented by cheap imports. BZW also reduced its forecast for RJB's pre-tax profits for this year to 192 million stg. The strength of sterling is seen as having a critical impact on the company's likely profit level.
-- NATWEST IN DEAL WITH PAYMENTS CARD GROUP

A deal has been announced between American Express and National Westminster Bank that will result in the latter being allowed to issue its own Amex brand card. The deal is seen as a major breakthrough for Amex into the lucrative European market and comes in the wake of a warning delivered to Visa by the European Commission over its efforts to prevent member banks issuing cards from rival groups. Though not exclusive, it is not expected that other UK banks will be joining Amex in the near future.
-- COLT PLANS EXPANSION AS SHARES RISE 13 PER CENT ON DEBUT

Colt Communications, the telecoms company offering services to businesses in the City of London, has seen its shares rise 13 per cent in value on their first day of trading. The company is hoping to raise about 190 million stg to fund planned expansion into other European financial centres. The success of the company's flotation came as a number of others announced they were postponing launch plans in the light of last week's market volatility.
-- EU ENTRANTS 'MUST SIGN UP FOR EMU'

A report from the European Parliament states that those countries wishing to join the ranks of the European Union will be obliged to support Emu and to adopt the policies necessary to prepare their economies for participation in the single currency. The report also outlines a number of political as well as economic challenges facing not only aspirant members but also the EU itself in relation to plans for expansion. Structural funds and agricultural policies within the EU will need to be reformed if expansion costs are to be controlled.
-- ICL STRENGTHENS MICROSOFT TIES

The UK computer group ICL, a division of Fujitsu, is reported to be planning to bolster its links with US software giant Microsoft, committing itself to support of the Windows NT operating system. The expected decision comes at a time when ICL's own main operating system, VME, is coming to the end of its useful life. ICL's decision is seen as an acceptance that NT is set to become the operating system standard for corporate network users. Microsoft already has a number of NT alliances with other companies, such as Digital Equipment.
-- BRUSSELS URGED TO RESEARCH V-CHIP

Britain's National Heritage Secretary Virginia Bottomley, expressing once more the government's concern about levels of sex and violence on TV screens, has called upon the European Union to embark on research into the V-chip, a computer device which supporters believe will provide the means for parents to control the type of TV content their children view. The call came as a report suggested that the technology involved in the chip still required considerable development.
-- MOST CONSUMERS SAY THEY WOULD LIKE MORE GREEN PRODUCTS

A report from the National Consumer Council has noted that, while consumers may sometimes overstate their concern for the environment, there is a genuine demand among the general public for so-called "green" products. Research carried out by the council found that 55 per cent of the population wanted to see a greater range of such products. However, the same survey found that a considerable proportion of the population does not actually believe that they can do very much that will help protect the environment.
-- INSURERS CLAIM CONCESSIONS ON PREMIUM TAX

British insurance companies are reported to have secured a number of concessions from the government over its planned increase in taxes on insurance premiums. The most recent Budget saw Kenneth Clarke reveal plans for an increase in this tax from 2.5 per cent to 4 per cent. He also revealed plans for increased VAT charges on travel and loan protection insurance. It is believed that one of the concessions secured is the removal of this higher rate of VAT from loan protection insurance.
